question: After resolving current-main conflicts, should maintainers land this structured `bypassCronDelivery` fix with focused validation, or require live Telegram proof first?
rationale: The code direction is the right layer, but the branch is dirty and the change intentionally suppresses user-channel delivery for a new fatal cron signal, so maintainers should own the refresh and proof bar before merge.

options.title: Refresh And Validate
options.body: Rebase or merge current main, preserve the cron delivery-awareness path, rerun the focused cron and embedded-runner validation, then proceed if no new defects appear.

options.title: Require Telegram Proof
options.body: Hold merge until Mantis or equivalent live Telegram proof shows the self-debug text is not sent to the topic.

options.title: Reopen Direction Discussion
options.body: Pause this PR only if maintainers want a different delivery disposition than full no-dispatch for exhausted unavailable-tool cron failures.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Validate
recommendation.body: Rebase or merge current main, preserve the cron delivery-awareness path, rerun the focused cron and embedded-runner validation, then proceed if no new defects appear.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned repository-member author of the active fix branch and can best refresh the dirty PR while preserving intent.
